page: Google Cloud Platform n1-highmem-2 is a general-purpose virtual machine configuration engineered with an elevated memory-to-vCPU allocation. The instance provides 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical core across 2 hyperthreads on a 2.3 GHz Intel Xeon processor. It includes 13.0 GB of system memory, yielding 6.5 GB of RAM per vCPU. The x86_64 CPU features 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.25 MB of L2 cache, and 45 MB of shared L3 cache, with hardware support for AVX, AES-NI, and BMI2 instructions. It does not bundle local storage disks or integrated GPU hardware, and complimentary public IPv4 networking addresses are not included.

Benchmark evaluations position the compute and memory subsystem within the lower performance tiers compared to newer cloud architecture. The server achieved a Geekbench single-core score of 944.0 and a multi-core score of 1124.0, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 1722.55 and a memory benchmark score of 1423.0. In synthetic throughput assessments, uncached 256 MB memory transfers registered 13.32 GB/s for reads and 11.13 GB/s for writes. Application-level metrics demonstrate a Redis SET throughput of 1.38 million operations per second and a static web serving transfer rate of 1.58 GB/s.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n1-highmem-2 offers an economical profile for applications needing a high ratio of memory without scaling up core counts. The primary tradeoff lies in the older generation processing cores, which exhibit limited single-threaded computational power and constrained instruction set capabilities, lacking newer extensions like AVX-512. The configuration is appropriate for lightweight caching layers, small in-memory key-value stores, staging databases, and background batch jobs that require a modest memory buffer under low compute loads.
description: Google Cloud Platform n1-highmem-2 is a memory-leaning instance offering 2 vCPUs on 1 physical Intel Xeon core running at 2.3 GHz, paired with 13.0 GB of memory. Based on the x86_64 architecture with AVX and AES extensions, the configuration omits local physical storage and dedicated GPU acceleration. Benchmark assessments place its processing capabilities in the lower tiers, registering a Geekbench multi-core score of 1124.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 1722.55. Memory bandwidth reaches 13.32 GB/s on uncached reads, while Redis operations reach 1.38 million SET operations per second. The instance provides an economical solution for memory-skewed setups that do not demand aggressive compute execution, making it suitable for small in-memory datastores, lightweight caching services, background workers, and low-traffic web applications.
